Brutal. | Echoes of Ancestral Threads
item.description: Amy Leigh Braaf is a South African artist, who intricately explores self-discovery and complexities of love through her art, drawing from the nation's biodiversity. Her pieces symbolize the navigation of her identity as a woman of mixed Cape Malay and Indonesian heritage. Braaf’s journey encapsulates cultural heritage, self-discovery, and timeless connections, resonating as an ode to human existence, weaving stories of generations past and present into an evocative dance of life.

item.title: RMB Latitudes 2026 | Nigeria Focus
item.description: RMB Latitudes 2026 Presents Nigeria Focus Each year, RMB Latitudes Art Fair spotlights one African country through its International Focus programme, fostering exchange and visibility across the continent. In 2026, the programme turns to Nigeria, bringing together more than 30 artists working across painting, photography, textile and sculpture. As one of the most expansive presentations of contemporary Nigerian practice within a cross-continental framework, Nigeria Focus reflects a breadth of voices and approaches rarely brought together between West and Southern Africa. Nigeria Focus unfolds as a cross-border exhibition, beginning in Lagos (15 April 2026) and culminating at RMB Latitudes Art Fair in Johannesburg (22–24 May 2026). The Lagos presentation offers a curated preview of selected artists, situating the works within their local context before the full exhibition is presented in Johannesburg, connecting audiences, collectors and institutions across West and Southern Africa. item.title: Notes from the Fire
item.description: In a world defined by acceleration and consumption, what does it mean to leave a mark? Notes from the Fire is a multidisciplinary solo exhibition by Givan Lötz. Presenting work of visual speculative fiction, Lötz imagines a time after time. Wax, casting, and surface serve as residues of a world forged in fire — an enduring imprint of heat, loss, and survival. Set within the speculative era of the Pyrocene, the exhibition unfolds as a fragmented archive of the future. Carbonised artefacts, coded surfaces, and partial systems speak to a reality in which knowledge is no longer stable, and meaning must be excavated rather than consumed. With surfaces cryptic and functions opaque, Notes from the Fire invites reflection and curiosity from its audience, presenting traces of a world disturbingly familiar yet wonderfully strange. The exhibition gestures toward the urgency of climate collapse driven by human consequences, while resisting complete moral closure and resolution. Instead, it holds space for endurance where something stubbornly human remains: the impulse to mark, to remember, to leave a signal in the ashes.

item.title: Above and Beyond
item.description: RMB Latitudes Art Fair presents a Special Project by featured artist Dada Khanyisa (b. 1991, Umzimkhulu; lives in Cape Town). Titled Above and Beyond, the exhibition is positioned in one of the Fair's most distinctive architectural spaces, the Turret. Khanyisa's practice centres on sculptural paintings and painted wooden assemblages that move between painting, collage and low-relief sculpture. Drawing from everyday social moments and contemporary South African life, Khanyisa transforms intimate interactions into reflections on broader dynamics – from youth culture to community and belonging. The particular site specific installation, comprised of a number of different panels, draws on pop cultural references and memories particular to a young Black adult navigating leisure in Cape Town, Southj Africa. Rendered in the midst of tensions and passion, Khanyisa liberates their figures from the typical idylic stillness of the fine art subject.
